title: KNOWN_LANGUAGE_CATEGORIES hardcoded to rust/dart — noise in other workspaces
description:
src/lessons.rs:192 hardcodes KNOWN_LANGUAGE_CATEGORIES = ["rust", "dart"]. The Phase 3 filter only excludes a lesson when its language tags are recognized AS language tags and none match the workspace.

Consequence: in a Python or TypeScript workspace, a lesson tagged `python` has no recognized language tag, so `lang_tags.is_empty()` is true and it passes unconditionally — and so does every rust/dart lesson if the workspace language list doesn't line up. Once write-boundary surfacing (sutra/276) runs in non-manas repos this turns the guard into a noise generator.

Derive the language category set from the indexed language adapters rather than a literal.

acceptance_criteria.text: Language category set derived from available language adapters, not a hardcoded literal
Rust-tagged lesson does not surface in a workspace with no Rust files
Test covering a language tag outside the current hardcoded pair

execution_record:
LANGUAGE_CATEGORIES is now a LazyLock built from default_registry().language_ids() (added LanguageRegistry::language_ids()). Alignment argument: remember::enrich seeds language categories from `file.language` lowercased, which is exactly an adapter's language_id — verified against the indexed corpus, where distinct files.language values across ~12 workspaces are exactly rust/dart/python.

Found and fixed a second latent bug in the same block that the task description did not anticipate: is_language_category compared case-insensitively but the workspace membership test used exact equality on a HashSet<&str>. A "Rust"-tagged lesson would therefore be recognised as language-tagged and then fail to match a workspace reporting "rust" — dropping the lesson from its own language's workspace. Both sides are lowercased now.

Test coverage: the existing suite already covered rust-vs-dart exclusion, uncategorised-everywhere, and technology-tag-everywhere, so I trimmed the new tests down to the four genuinely uncovered cases (non-rust/dart language tag, python workspace, case-insensitive match, OR semantics across multiple language tags) and reused the existing lang_ctx helper rather than adding a second one.

Verification beyond the suite passing: temporarily reverted is_language_category to the hardcoded pair in place and confirmed language_tag_outside_the_formerly_hardcoded_pair_is_filtered fails with the old behaviour, then restored. Note that rust_tag_filtered_out_of_a_python_workspace passes under BOTH old and new code — "rust" was already in the literal — so it guards the invariant without demonstrating the bug.

Scope note: this is preventative today. The lessons store currently holds no python/js/ts-tagged lessons (only rust=41, dart=13), so no live leak was observed. It becomes load-bearing as soon as lessons are captured in a non-Rust/Dart repo, which sutra/276 makes likely.

1446 tests pass, clippy clean on touched files, guard E2E re-verified after the change.
root_cause: Phase 3 category filtering is subtractive: it only excludes a lesson when the lesson's tags are recognised as language tags AND none match the workspace. Recognition ran off a hardcoded KNOWN_LANGUAGE_CATEGORIES = ["rust","dart"], so any other language tag (python, typescript, ...) fell through the `lang_tags.is_empty() -> return true` branch and the lesson was treated as language-neutral rather than as belonging to a language. The failure mode is inverted from what the literal suggests: an unlisted language leaks everywhere instead of being filtered nowhere.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (range 6369fc3..91fedc7) — verdict: approve with notes; the fix is correct as far as it goes.

Verified: LANGUAGE_CATEGORIES now derives from default_registry().language_ids() = {rust, dart, c, python, javascript, typescript}, lowercased on both the recognition and the matching side (the case-asymmetry bug the comment describes is genuinely closed).

[medium] Fail-open on unrecognized tags is unchanged, so the class of bug persists for alias tags. is_language_category matches only exact adapter language_ids. A lesson tagged `ts`, `js`, `py`, `golang`, `cpp`, or any language sutra has no adapter for still produces lang_tags.is_empty() == true and passes unconditionally into every workspace. remember::enrich seeds from file.language so its own writes line up, but tags supplied by a caller do not have to. Once sutra/276's write-boundary surfacing runs in non-manas repos this is still a noise vector, just a narrower one.
Suggested follow-up: either an alias table mapping common shorthands to adapter ids, or flip the default so a tag that looks like a language but is unrecognized is treated as a language claim (fail closed) rather than as language-neutral.

[low] Cross-task interaction: src/guard.rs:405 language_from_path still hardcodes rust/dart, so the adapter-derived set here is broader than what the guard can actually produce imports for. See sutra/276 review comment.
